channel.title: SolCrys — AEO guides and news
channel.description: SolCrys helps marketing teams turn AI answer gaps into governed content, citation, and marketplace actions they can approve, ship, and verify.

item.title: Models Change. The Harness Compounds.
item.description: Eason Wang, SolCrys CPO, on why the model isn't the moat, bought or fine-tuned, and what compounds instead: model portfolios, scenario evals, a harness.

item.title: The AI Citation Window Is Closing: Why AEO Timing Beats Tactics
item.description: The sources an AI trusts for a category narrow over time toward two or three brands. While that pool is still open, getting cited is cheap; once it freezes around incumbents, displacing an anchor costs far more. So AEO has a first-mover dynamic, and the strategic question isn't only what to do, it's whether your category's citation window is still open.

item.title: Search, Agent, or Training? How to Set AI Crawler Access in 2026 Without Blocking Your Own Citations
item.description: Which AI crawlers to allow, what Cloudflare's Sept. 15, 2026 rules changed, and how to block AI training without losing your AI citations.

item.title: Discover in AI, Decide on Your Site: What AI-Referred Buyers Need From the Page They Land On
item.description: AI answers shape the shortlist, but B2B decisions still close on your site. A 5-part checklist for the page AI-referred buyers land on, and how to measure it.

item.title: AI Search in 2026: A Dated Timeline and the Statistics That Hold Up (With Source, Date, and Sample)
item.description: 28 AI search statistics for 2026, each with source, date, and sample, plus a dated timeline of the year and the widely quoted numbers to stop using.

item.title: ChatGPT Ads Don't Buy the Answer: How to Budget and Report Sponsored vs. Organic AI Visibility
item.description: ChatGPT ads sit below the answer; OpenAI says they don't influence it. How to budget ads beside AEO and report organic and sponsored AI visibility apart.

item.title: Google Now Calls AI-Answer Manipulation Spam. The GEO Tactics That Cross the Line—and the Ones That Just Don't Work.
item.description: Google's spam policies now cover manipulating AI answers. Which GEO tactics cross the line, which are risky, which are wasted, and what holds up.

item.title: Every Model Upgrade Is a Migration: The Harness Marketing Teams Need Before the Next One
item.description: Model releases now land every few weeks. Jia Chang, SolCrys CTO, on running each one as a migration, with a 10-step checklist for marketing AI workflows.

item.title: The Free AI Reports: What Search Console, Bing, GA4, and Merchant Center Show, and What None of Them Do
item.description: Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, GA4, and Merchant Center now report AI search for free. What each one shows, what it misses, and how to cover the gaps.

item.title: What Is AI SEO? AI SEO vs AEO vs GEO, and What Actually Changes in 2026
item.description: AI SEO, AEO, and GEO name one job: getting cited in AI answers. Where each term came from, what Google says, and why the engine matters more than the name.

item.title: A Year in View: The Models Kept Changing. The Facts Had to Hold.
item.description: Eason Wang on year one of answer engine optimization: how buyers, engines, and models changed, what we built and deleted, and 5 predictions for year two.

item.title: Your Brand, AI Ready: One Year of SolCrys
item.description: SolCrys co-founder and CEO Gwen Chen on year one — why AI is now the first reader of your brand, and how one Corporate Context came to power AI answers, webpages, booth animation, and community engagement for the teams we work with.

item.title: Community Intelligence: reading the communities AI engines read
item.description: How SolCrys turns citation evidence into a Reddit targeting playbook, scores threads for subject fit, drafts replies against each subreddit's own rules, and stops at the clipboard. No API-post path exists.

item.title: Signal: a weekly market brief tied to the prompts you are losing
item.description: Signal scans your configured sources each week, ranks what changed, de-dupes against recent weeks, and binds every idea to a tracked AEO prompt - so the only ideas promoted to work are the ones aimed at a prompt you are measurably losing.

item.title: Running an AEO practice across a book of clients
item.description: The weekly operating rhythm of a multi-client AEO practice: what is shared across the book, what has to be per client, where a solo operator breaks, and what the two agency tiers actually buy.

item.title: Ranking but Not Cited
item.description: You rank well and still aren't cited in AI answers. Here are the five gaps SEO leaves — per-engine citation, corroboration, extractability, accuracy, and measurement — and how to close each.

item.title: Announcing the SolCrys Corporate Context Engine
item.description: Today we're introducing the SolCrys Corporate Context Engine — a living record of your company that keeps AI current as your business evolves.

item.title: Prove AI Influence with Closed-Won Interviews
item.description: Your dashboard says branded search. Your buyers say ChatGPT. The fastest defensible way to prove AI influence on pipeline is a monthly closed-won interview — the script, the sample size, the CRM field, and the 1-in-X readout that gets AEO funded.

item.title: Identity and Capability: The Agentic Web Still Runs on Being Chosen
item.description: The agentic web is splitting into an identity layer and a capability layer. Neither fires until an answer engine chooses your brand first. Here is the order of operations, and why AEO is the precondition for both.

item.title: The Future of Answer Engine Optimization Is Human
item.description: A frontier model can't do your AEO for you — not because the models are weak, but because your category has no visible board. Why winning the answer engines is a human-plus-AI problem, and why that's good news.

item.title: AEO for Investors: Diligence Now Starts with an AI Answer
item.description: Investors now run market maps, competitor scans, and first-pass diligence through ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Copilot. If AI doesn't know your startup exists, or describes it wrong, you can be screened out before the first meeting. How to audit and fix what answer engines say about your company before you raise.

item.title: The New E-E-A-T: Where Experience, Expertise, Authority & Trust Actually Live in AI Search
item.description: E-E-A-T isn't dead in AI search, it moved. The four qualities still decide whether AI recommends you, but they're no longer signaled on your own page, they're established across the sources the model trusts. How each of experience, expertise, authoritativeness, and trust relocates for AEO.

item.title: Owned, Earned, Paid: How Your Media Mix Maps to AI Visibility (and Why the Hierarchy Flips)
item.description: The owned/earned/paid split you use for marketing maps onto AI visibility with one twist: the hierarchy flips. In an AI answer, trust runs inverse to control, the sources you own are trusted least, the independent ones you can't buy are trusted most. A map of each layer and where to focus.

item.title: Do Sponsored Articles Move AI Answers? What Paid Placements on TechTarget, Forbes & CIO Actually Buy You
item.description: A sponsored article on TechTarget, Forbes, or CIO.com can change what AI says about you, but not the way a paid-media plan assumes. It works only when the domain is one the model already cites and the content reads as editorial, not an ad. Then it's a corroboration asset, not impressions. How to tell the difference, and measure it.

item.title: Your Best Proof Is Trapped in Private AI Chats. Here's How to Make It Public.
item.description: There's a specific reason your 'why we're the best' page does nothing in AI answers, and why a great specialist product stays invisible: the model discounts what you say about yourself, and your real proof happens in private chats and emails it can't read. How to move the private conclusion your customers already reached into public, in their words.

item.title: AEO for PR: How to Prove Your Earned Media Actually Moved the AI Answer
item.description: Earned media is the single most powerful AEO lever a brand has, because it's the corroboration layer AI trusts, but PR measurement wasn't built to see it. How comms teams measure whether a campaign, announcement, or media hit actually changed what AI says, with a clean before/after.

item.title: Your Star Rating Gets You Shown in AI Answers. Your Review Text Gets You Picked.
item.description: Star ratings reach AI answers through licensed or first-party data, such as Yelp in ChatGPT. Review text explains the pick. How to earn both within the rules.

item.title: AI Recommendation Score
item.description: AI can name your brand and recommend a rival in the next sentence. The Recommendation Score grades every AI answer 0-100 on how favorably it positions you across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Claude, plots you against every competitor, and shows the verbatim line behind every point.

item.title: Contested, Settling, or Decaying? Turn AI-Citation Variance Into a Spend Decision
item.description: The contested-vs-settled signal tells you which AI queries are winnable. This is how to act on it: measure the noise floor per query, classify each query's phase, route each phase to a different move, and avoid the trap that wrecks the whole thing, mistaking a query that's dying for one you're losing.

item.title: AI Doesn't Cite a Neutral Web. It Cites an Incentive Map.
item.description: AI leans on third-party sources to decide what's true about your brand, but those sources aren't neutral. Each one carries an incentive that predicts the way it bends the truth about you. How to read the source set behind your AI answers as an incentive map, and win the sources whose incentive aligns with you.
